See also: Septembre

Catalan

[edit]

Noun

[edit]

septembre m (plural septembres)

  1. obsolete form of setembre

Further reading

[edit]
  • “septembre” in Diccionari català-valencià-balear, Antoni Maria Alcover and Francesc de Borja Moll, 1962.

Cimbrian

[edit]

Alternative forms

[edit]
  • septembar (Sette Comuni)

Etymology

[edit]

From Middle High German september, from Latin September. Cognate with German September.

Noun

[edit]

septembre m

  1. (Luserna) September
    Synonyms: zibante maanont, herbestmånat

See also

[edit]
Gregorian calendar months (Luserna dialect)edit
  • djenaro, hochnach
  • fevraro, hornung
  • martzo, lentz
  • abrèl, aprile
  • madjo
  • sunjo, prachmånat
  • ludjo, höbiat
  • agosto, snittmånat
  • septembre, herbestmånat
  • otobre, bimmat
  • novembre, bintarmånat
  • ditzembre, kristmånat

References

[edit]
  • “septembre” in Martalar, Umberto Martello; Bellotto, Alfonso (1974), Dizionario della lingua Cimbra dei Sette Communi vicentini, 1st edition, Roana, Italy: Instituto di Cultura Cimbra A. Dal Pozzo

French

[edit]

Alternative forms

[edit]
  • sept. (abbreviation)

Etymology

[edit]

Borrowed from Latin Septembrem. Cf. Old French setembre, sietembre.

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • IPA(key): /sɛp.tɑ̃bʁ/
  • Audio:(file)
  • (dated) IPA(key): /sɛ.tɑ̃bʁ/ ~ /se.tɑ̃bʁ/
  • (Louisiana) IPA(key): /sɛp.tɔ̃m/, /sɛk.tɔ̃m/
  • Audio (France (Paris)):(file)
  • Audio (France (Vosges)):(file)
  • Audio (France (Massy)):(file)

Noun

[edit]

septembre m (plural septembres)

  1. September

Derived terms

[edit]
  • mi-septembre

Descendants

[edit]
  • Guianese Creole: sèptanm
  • Haitian Creole: septanm
  • → Iranian Persian: سپتامبر (septâmbr)
  • → South Azerbaijani: سئپتامبر (septambr)
  • → Tunisian Arabic: سبتمبر (septōmbr)
